name: Undersea cables & GPS
value: SMW5 cable fault off Pakistan since 18 Nov
summary: A fault on the SMW5 cable off Pakistan cut traffic by up to 36% from 18 Nov; cause not identified, no sabotage confirmed
state: Pakistan's telecoms authority linked slow internet and outages from 18 Nov to a fault about 11km off the coast in the SMW5 submarine cable; Cloudflare Radar said HTTP traffic fell by as much as 36%, traffic was rerouted and no cause or repair time was given (The National, 18–19 Nov). Searches on 27 Nov found no restoration announcement for this fault. A cable damage incident keeps Watch; no multiple cuts isolating a region or confirmed sabotage was found.
for_you: Internet users and businesses in Pakistan may see slower international connections while traffic is rerouted; repairs at sea typically take days to weeks.
rubric_hit: Watch: cable damage incident (SMW5 fault off Pakistan, 18 Nov); no confirmed sabotage

sources.title: The National — Pakistan internet problems after SMW5 subsea cable fault

why: Subsea cables carry ~99% of intercontinental data; GPS jamming affects aviation and shipping.
drivers: Anchor drags, sabotage, conflict-zone jamming and spoofing.

rubric.alert: Multiple cable cuts isolating a region, or confirmed sabotage.
rubric.watch: Cable damage incident, or widespread GNSS interference affecting aviation.
rubric.normal: No new cable cuts or major jamming escalations.
